column1: # THE SECONDARY SWEEP, RULING R15 part 2 (f) to (j) of 2026-09-08. One job per cell of
# record, judge Qwen3-32B at revision 9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137 on its
# PINNED a100-80 line (section 6.1), Q1 file q1_mention_2026-09-07d.md, gate and Q2 files
# unchanged, completion budget 1,024 tokens, experiments/jury/runner.py --mode audit,
# which is section 6.4's sweep protocol: one run per item plus a seeded 10 percent that
# gets three. Every vote is stamped configuration=secondary-qwen3-32b-d-np1024 and
# secondary=true. What this produces is a raw judge-labelled Q1 disclosure share per cell,
# printed BESIDE column A of record (the frozen regex share) and never selected on.
# The 16 cells are the ones whose subject is Gemma-2-9B-it or Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The
# eight Qwen3-8B cells are excluded by (f): section 6.2's own-family exclusion binds a
# single judge exactly as it binds a panel, so the Qwen judge has no task on a Qwen
# subject and BCF_ALL_JUDGE_ROWS is therefore NOT set on any row here.
# BEFORE SUBMITTING, three things, none of which this file can do for you:
#   1. Build the items. For each cell,
#        PYTHONPATH=src python -m experiments.jury.sweep_items \
#          --transcripts ~/bcf/results/<model>/<substrate>/<cue>/transcripts.jsonl
#      writes ~/bcf/jury-items/<model>/<substrate>/<cue>/items.jsonl and manifest.json,
#      which are the two paths every row below names. The job REFUSES with exit 15 if the
#      manifest is missing, does not say "secondary": true, or does not carry the sha256
#      of the items file it was handed.
#   2. Sync this branch to /home/e/e1506804/bcf/repo-jury-secondary and submit with
#        BCF_JURY_SBATCH=/home/e/e1506804/bcf/repo-jury-secondary/bcf/judge_serve.sbatch \
#          bcf/jury_wave.sh --dry-run bcf/judges_secondary_a100.tsv
#      That tree has to carry experiments/jury/sweep_items.py, a judge_serve.sbatch that
#      knows BCF_JURY_MODE, a runner.py with --secondary, prompt d, and the newer env.sh
#      that defines bcf_pick_port and bcf_wait_server_ready. ~/bcf/repo-jury has none of
#      the first four. Check it with
#        grep -l BCF_JURY_MODE <tree>/bcf/judge_serve.sbatch && ls <tree>/experiments/jury/sweep_items.py
#   3. SUBMIT AT MOST THE LIVE a100-80 HEADROOM AT A TIME. The per-user a100-80 cap is 4
#      cards counting every campaign on the account, so jury_wave.sh refuses all 16 rows
#      at once and submits nothing. Pass a sliced copy of this file (4 rows or fewer) and
#      keep the rest here for the record.
# WALL AND RESUME. 02:50:00 on every row, which fits partition gpu's 3 hour ceiling as
# well as gpu-long's 72 (jury_wave.sh routes a100-80 to gpu-long), and BCF_RESUME=1 on
# every row so a second leg picks up from votes.jsonl. Audit mode costs 5 votes per item
# and 11 on the seeded tenth, so a cell of n items plans 5n + 6 x round(0.1n) votes. At
# the measured 0.49 votes per second (job 829038, 4,800 votes in 3:00:20) and about 20
# minutes of model load, one leg judges about 4,410 votes. The eight STATED-HINT and
# PROFESSOR cells are all above that and need a second leg (the largest, the two 1,380
# item arc_challenge cells, plan 7,728 votes and want 4h22 of judging); the eight
# METADATA and GRADER-CODE cells finish in one leg each. 71,297 votes over the 16 cells,
# 40h25 of judging, about 48h25 of card time over 24 legs.
# JUDGE_KEYS
